extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, patent examiners, and patent drafters (attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting and examining patent claims to ensure every claim term has proper antecedent basis and is unambiguous with respect to the specification and other claims. Covers article usage, dependent-claim references, number agreement, inherent components, and best-practice reconciliation of claims and specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antecedent basis requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All terms in a claim must be properly introduced before being modified or referenced; claim terms must find clear support or antecedent basis in the specification so that the meaning of the terms may be ascertainable by reference to the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure every claim term can be traced to an earlier recitation in the claims or to the specification so its meaning is ascertainable. Lack of antecedent basis can create clarity/indefiniteness problems, though absence of identical wording in the specification does not automatically render a term indefinite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article usage when introducing and referring to elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Use indefinite article 'a' or 'an' when introducing an element for the first time; use definite article 'the' or 'said' when referring back to the introduced element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce elements with 'a' or 'an' (e.g., 'a lever') on first recitation; thereafter refer back with 'the', 'said', or 'such'. Consistently follow this convention throughout the claim to show antecedent relationship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on definite/demonstrative articles prior to introduction
rubrics_metrics.description: The definite articles 'the,' 'said,' and 'such' cannot be used unless the noun has already been introduced in the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use 'the', 'said', or 'such' to introduce a noun; they are only appropriate when the noun has a prior antecedent recitation in the claim (or in an incorporated claim).

rubrics_metrics.name: Antecedent basis in dependent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: In a dependent claim, the antecedent basis should be present in that dependent claim or any claim upon which that claim is dependent (since a dependent claim incorporates all of the claims from which it depends, by reference).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When drafting dependent claims, ensure any terms introduced are either present in the dependent claim itself or in the claim(s) it depends from; check the claim dependency chain for proper antecedent support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid ambiguous references when multiple similar elements exist
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not refer back with a phrase such as 'said lever' when two different levers (or other duplicate-type elements) have been recited earlier and the reference would be ambiguous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple similar elements are present, use distinguishing language (e.g., 'first lever', 'second lever') or explicitly specify which element is being referenced to avoid ambiguity in antecedent reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number agreement between singular and plural recitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Plural nouns must agree in number with the earlier recitation (e.g., avoid 'said widgets' when only one 'widget' was introduced).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain number agreement—introduce singular or plural as appropriate and ensure later references use matching singular/plural forms to preserve clear antecedent basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antecedent basis vs. identical wording in the specification
rubrics_metrics.description: The mere fact that a term has no antecedent basis in the specification disclosure does not necessarily mean the term is indefinite; there is no requirement that the words in the claim must match those used in the specification disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims may use different wording than the specification so long as the meaning is ascertainable by reference to the specification; do not assume lack of identical terms in the spec automatically causes indefiniteness—assess whether the claim term has clear support or is reasonably understandable in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inherent components have antecedent basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Inherent components of recited elements have antecedent basis in the recitation of the elements themselves (e.g., 'a wheel' inherently has 'a hub' and 'a rim').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that commonplace or inherent parts of a recited element may be treated as having antecedent basis by virtue of the element's recitation; use this principle cautiously and only where the components are truly inherent and ascertainable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting best practices to avoid antecedent problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Review and reconcile both the specification and claims; first introduction uses 'a'/'an' and later references use 'the'/'said'; avoid implicit antecedence where ambiguous; antecedent problems are typically drafting oversights easily corrected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform a claims/spec reconciliation pass to locate and fix missing antecedents, eliminate implicit antecedence, add explicit identifiers for repeated elements, and correct article/number usage. Treat antecedent issues as correctable drafting errors before filing or during prosecution.
